# a11y-audit

> Open, self-hosted accessibility regression evidence for large web estates.
> Template-aware sampling, stable finding fingerprints, and accepted
> baselines let CI block new barriers without requiring zero existing debt.

## What this skill does

- Scans web projects for accessibility violations using axe-core, with evidence matrices for WCAG 2.1 AA (default), WCAG 2.2 AA, and EN 301 549 clause 9
- Discovers site structure via sitemap.xml (or HTML crawl fallback)
- Classifies pages into template groups and selects representatives
- Produces structured reports with prioritized findings and fix guidance
- Tracks progress between audits (delta comparison)
- Creates reviewable accepted baselines and can fail CI only on new findings
- Auto-installs its own dependencies (axe-core, Puppeteer)

## Where it fits

- Use Storybook or authored Playwright tests for component and interaction coverage.
- Use this project for repository-native evidence across large route and template sets.
- Use an enterprise platform for hosted monitoring, program dashboards, and managed manual testing.

## Boundaries

- Automated evidence does not certify WCAG or legal conformance.
- The skill reports findings and guidance; it does not modify application source.
- It does not provide hosted monitoring, VPAT generation, or screen-reader simulation.

## How to use

Install (simplest first): (1) have your assistant fetch, GuideCheck-verify, and follow https://skilla11y.dev/.well-known/assistant-guide.txt with per-action approval; or (2) `npx skills add snapsynapse/skill-a11y-audit --skill a11y-audit`.
Claude Code project skills live in `.claude/skills/`; Codex project skills
live in `.agents/skills/`.

Prompt: "Run an accessibility audit on this project."

Or run scripts directly:

- `scripts/discover.js --url <base-url>` — discover pages and select representatives
- `scripts/scan.js --urls <url-list>` — scan pages with axe-core
- `scripts/scan.js --urls <url-list> --baseline <file> --fail-on new` — run a regression gate
- `scripts/report.js --input <scan.json>` — generate markdown + JSON report
- `scripts/report.js --input <scan.json> --standard wcag22-aa` — switch the evidence matrix (wcag21-aa, wcag22-aa, en301549)

## Key files

- [Assistant Guide](https://skilla11y.dev/.well-known/assistant-guide.txt): bounded assistant install, audit execution, and maintenance instructions
- [SKILL.md](a11y-audit/SKILL.md): core skill instructions (agent-readable)
- [scripts/](a11y-audit/scripts/): discover.js, scan.js, report.js, bootstrap-context.js, plan-issues.js
- [references/output-contract.md](a11y-audit/references/output-contract.md): report format specification
- [references/output-schema.json](a11y-audit/references/output-schema.json): JSON output schema
- [assets/sample-output/](a11y-audit/assets/sample-output/): example report from a real site audit
- [CHANGELOG.md](a11y-audit/CHANGELOG.md): version history
- [MANIFEST.yaml](a11y-audit/MANIFEST.yaml): bundle inventory

## Report sections

1. Executive Summary (severity counts)
2. Findings by Rule (violation details, WCAG mapping)
3. Quick Fixes (one-liner remediation per rule)
4. Color Contrast Details (exact ratios and selectors)
5. Standards Automated Evidence Matrix (WCAG 2.1 AA default, WCAG 2.2 AA, or EN 301 549 via --standard; not certification)
6. Delta from Previous Audit (fixed, new, changed)
7. Remediation Priority (ranked by severity)
8. Sampling Strategy (template groups and coverage)
9. Shared Template Patterns (which groups share issues)

## Output modes

- `markdown` — report only
- `markdown+json` — report + machine-readable data
- `markdown+issues` — report + GitHub/GitLab/Linear/Jira tickets

## Compatibility

- Claude Code (tested, primary target)
- OpenAI Codex (tested)
- Any agent that reads markdown skill files
